Oil and gas NDT training in Houston: the short answer

Short answer: Atlantis NDT trains Houston inspection contractors, refinery and chemical plant crews and fabrication shops to ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. We do not run a Houston classroom. Theory is delivered live online, practicals run onsite at your facility on real specimens under an ASNT Level III, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Houston is crowded with established NDT schools, so this section does not pretend to be another one. It is written for the employer who needs a crew upgraded to Level II before turnaround season without sending six people across town for a week, for the inspection company that needs a Level III to fix its written practice before an operator audit, and for the working technician who wants instructor-led theory in the evenings while staying on the job. If you want a full-time campus programme, Houston has good ones, and they are listed honestly further down.

If you already know what you need, request a Houston oil and gas training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Oil and gas NDT work in Houston

The Houston Ship Channel and the bay shore around it hold one of the world's largest concentrations of refining and petrochemical capacity. Refineries and chemical complexes in Baytown, Deer Park, Pasadena, Channelview, La Porte and Texas City run inspection programmes that keep certified technicians busy year-round, and spike sharply during spring and autumn turnarounds when units come down for planned maintenance. Each turnaround brings thousands of inspection points: thickness readings at condition monitoring locations, weld examinations on repairs and new tie-ins, exchanger tube testing and vessel internals.

Behind the plants sits the fabrication belt: shops in the east and north Harris County corridors building pressure vessels, heat exchangers, process modules, skids and pipe spools for projects around the world. Their inspection work is new construction under ASME Section VIII and B31.3, with RT, UT and increasingly PAUT on welds and MT and PT on surfaces. Midstream adds pipeline and compressor station work under API 1104 and ASME B31.4 and B31.8, and the Gulf Coast LNG export terminals bring cryogenic stainless and nickel steel welding with heavy PT and RT demand. Offshore operators and their contractors, many headquartered in the Energy Corridor, add subsea and topsides scope.

Houston is also where most national inspection contractors have head offices or major branches. That matters for training because these firms run large SNT-TC-1A programmes, recruit constantly, and often prefer to upgrade technicians they already employ rather than hire new ones before a busy season.

Which NDT methods Houston oil and gas work uses, and under which rules

This table is context for planning training. The owner's specification and the contract always decide which code, edition and acceptance criteria apply.

MethodOil and gas application in HoustonCode or standard usually cited
UT (Level I, II, III)Thickness surveys at CMLs on piping and vessels; shear-wave weld examination on repairs and new constructionASME V Article 4 and 23; API 570 and 510 owner programmes; ASME VIII and B31.3 acceptance
PAUTTurnaround weld examination, corrosion mapping, RT replacement on fabrication welds where the code permitsASME V Article 4; ASME code cases and owner specifications
TOFDFlaw sizing on thick vessel and piping welds; in-service crack monitoringASME V; owner specification
RTPipe spool and vessel welds in fabrication; pipeline girth welds; profile RT for corrosion under insulationASME V Article 2; B31.3; API 1104
MTSurface cracking in wet H2S and caustic service; fabrication weld surfacesASME V Article 7; owner procedures
PTStainless and nickel alloy welds, especially in LNG and chemical serviceASME V Article 6
VTWeld visual inspection, vessel internals during turnarounds, fit-up checks in fabricationASME V Article 9; B31.3; AWS D1.1 for structural steel
ETHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing during turnarounds; surface crack detectionOwner specifications; ASME V Article 8

Method spotlight: PAUT and TOFD for turnaround welds. Turnaround schedules leave little time for film, and owners increasingly accept encoded PAUT, often paired with TOFD for sizing, on repair and tie-in welds. That has created steady demand for Level II PAUT technicians who also understand the underlying UT theory well enough to defend a scan plan. A crew upgrade that builds conventional UT to Level II first, then adds PAUT, is the most common request we see from Gulf Coast employers.

Which certification scheme Houston oil and gas employers expect

Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Other schemes appear below so you know what your employer may also ask for, not because we offer them.

SchemeWho in Houston requires itDoes SNT-TC-1A training fit?
ASNT SNT-TC-1A (employer-based)Inspection contractors, fabrication shops, refinery and chemical plant contractors, pipeline contractorsYes. It is the dominant scheme for NDT technicians in Houston, and what we train to.
Owner contractor-approval programmesRefineries and chemical plants that test or vet contract technicians before site accessYes as preparation. The owner's own practical tests sit on top of your employer certification.
API 510, 570 and 653 inspector certificationsOwner-user inspection departments for vessels, piping and tanksNo. These are API inspector credentials, separate from NDT technician certification. We do not offer API inspector training.
API QUTE and QUPASome owners require these API individual certification programmes for UT thickness or PAUT performancePartly. Strong SNT-TC-1A UT and PAUT training is the foundation; the API programmes are separate exams we do not provide.
AWS Certified Welding InspectorFabrication shops and owner QA for weld inspection leadsNo. CWI is a separate AWS credential that we do not train.
ISO 9712International projects and some foreign operatorsNo. ISO 9712 is a central certification scheme; we train to SNT-TC-1A only.

For most Houston technicians the order of priority is clear: a solid employer-certified SNT-TC-1A Level II in the methods your company bills, then the owner and API add-ons your clients require.

The SNT-TC-1A certification path for Houston technicians, step by step

  1. Your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A is employer-based; each company's written practice sets training hours, experience, exams and who signs certifications. See written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Theory in the method and level. Recommended minimums are in our training requirements matrix; your written practice sets the actual hours.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged and supervised work on real components. In Houston, turnaround seasons can deliver a lot of experience quickly, provided it is documented as it happens.
  4. Examinations. General, specific and practical exams administered and graded by a Level III, with the practical on real specimens.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision and colour contrast checks on the written practice's schedule.
  6. Employer certification. Signed by your employer and valid under its written practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval the written practice defines.

For the full scheme see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing and TWIC for Houston crews

Texas is an NRC Agreement State, and the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program licenses industrial radiography companies and their sources. Texas rules for industrial radiography, in 25 TAC §289.255, also set training and certification requirements for individual radiographers and radiographer trainees that are separate from SNT-TC-1A. An RT method course from any provider does not satisfy those requirements by itself. Your radiation safety officer will tell you what your company's licence requires.

Ship Channel work brings one more credential. Refineries and terminals with marine docks, and other facilities regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, require a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) for unescorted access. Many Houston employers expect new hires to arrive with one, so apply early. Site-specific safety orientations, which most plants require before work begins, are run by the owners and their safety councils.

How Houston crews can take the training

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions on Central time with recorded review, scheduled in evenings or around rotating shifts. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III runs the course and the practical block at your shop or a clean area at the plant, using your equipment, procedures and, where possible, your own parts. Nobody leaves the job site for a week.
  • Employer cohorts. Multi-method programmes for a whole crew, quoted per cohort and timed around your work calendar.

Timing is everything in a turnaround economy. The best window to upgrade a crew is usually the quieter months before spring and autumn turnaround season, so the newly certified Level IIs are ready when the work arrives. Ask about a pre-turnaround crew upgrade in Houston.

What a Houston employer receives from an onsite course

Each technician leaves with a training record showing method, level, hours, dates, course outline and instructor; graded exam records where Atlantis administers exams under your written practice; a description of the practical specimens; and a note on any gaps between your procedures and the owner specifications you work to. Those records are built to drop straight into certification files, so an operator's contractor audit can trace every hour without a scramble.

Level III services and written practices for Houston NDT companies

Houston has a large number of small and mid-size inspection firms, and many of them run on a written practice that was copied years ago and never updated. We provide written practice development, procedure review against owner specifications, exam administration and ongoing Level III support, plus multi-method programmes through corporate NDT training and oil and gas corporate training. For local consulting, see NDT consulting in Houston, refining NDT consulting in Houston, ASNT Level III consulting in Houston and Level III of record in Houston. Book a Level III consultation before your next operator audit.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site, a storage tank and a welding workshop. It helps with set-up, scan coverage and indication recognition between theory sessions. It is practice only and never replaces the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who sets course content, administers and grades examinations where your written practice assigns that role to Atlantis, and reviews employer written practices.

Frequently asked questions about oil and gas NDT training in Houston

How do I get NDT certified in Houston?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete formal training and logged experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III and pass the vision test. Training can be a campus programme, a classroom course or live online with onsite practicals; your employer signs the certification.

Is there oil and gas NDT training in Houston I can do online?

Yes, for theory. Practical training and the practical exam must be on real specimens, which we run onsite at your employer.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Houston?

No. We deliver live online and onsite at employer facilities, which is why we suit crews that cannot leave the job.

Do you offer API 510, 570 or 653 training?

No. Those are API inspector certifications. We train NDT technicians to SNT-TC-1A.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice and existing experience. Recommended minimums are in our training requirements matrix; logged experience usually takes longer than classroom hours.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Texas?

The company needs a DSHS radiography licence, and radiographers and trainees must meet the Texas training and certification rules in 25 TAC §289.255.

Do I need a TWIC card for NDT jobs in Houston?

For unescorted access to MTSA-regulated facilities such as refinery docks and Ship Channel terminals, yes. Many employers expect one at hire.

What does oil and gas NDT training cost in Houston?

Quote on request. Cost depends on method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery and any Level III work. Request a Houston training quote and we reply within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training in Houston?

Only at approved schools and programmes. Atlantis does not claim that approval; several Houston campus schools do advertise approvals, so check with the VA or Workforce Solutions. Employer-paid training is the other common route. See sponsoring employee NDT certification.

Which NDT method pays best in Houston oil and gas?

Advanced UT methods such as PAUT and TOFD generally command more than basic methods, but pay varies by employer and season. See our NDT salary guide.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Houston employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A employer certification is the norm for NDT technicians on the Gulf Coast, with owner and API add-ons where required.

How do I prepare for the exams?

Study your employer's procedures, use mock questions such as our UT Level 2 practice questions, and practise set-ups on the Practical NDT simulator.
